messages.content: Change of plan for St. Louis: Daniel would rather take Amtrak, and my cousin is proposing Friday dinner near wherever we stay instead of Saturday lunch. The downtown Union Station option is now cheaper. Can you compare it with the Forest Park Hampton hold before it expires—total, arrival/dinner logistics, museum Saturday, breakfast/room basics, cancellation, and Sunday bags?

Quick comparison:

| Option | Est. total | Friday/Sunday train logistics | Saturday museum | Food, room basics, cancel |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Forest Park Hampton hold | $418 | 15-20 min rideshare from Gateway Station each way; dinner would mean going straight out to CWE/Forest Park after the train | Easiest: 5-8 min rideshare to Saint Louis Art Museum | Breakfast included; coffee + mini-fridge listed; one-bed room held; cancel by Dec. 6, 6 p.m.; bag storage likely |
| Drury Union Station downtown | $356 | 5 min rideshare or 10-12 min walk from station; simplest after Amtrak and on Sunday | 15-20 min rideshare each way, or MetroLink plus a walk | Breakfast included; coffee/fridge listed; one-bed room available; cancel by Dec. 7, noon; front-desk bag storage |

Downtown saves about $62 before Saturday transportation. After museum rideshares, the savings is probably more like $20-30, but the train arrival and Sunday departure are much easier.
How awkward is Saturday from Union Station if we don’t rent a car?

Not terrible. I would not plan on walking. The cleanest version is a rideshare to the museum Saturday morning and another back after lunch or dinner. MetroLink can work, but it adds a transfer/walk and is less relaxed if weather is cold.
And Friday dinner downtown has enough casual options after the train?

Yes. Union Station has several casual places, and there are easy downtown/Riverfront options a short rideshare away. It is a better setup for meeting your cousin Friday without asking everyone to migrate west after you arrive.
Then switch to Drury. Please cancel Forest Park, same one-bed and quiet-room notes if available.

Done. I switched the St. Louis hold to Drury Union Station for Dec. 8-10, refundable, estimated $356 with taxes. Notes added: one-bed room, quiet location away from elevator if possible. Breakfast, in-room coffee, and refrigerator are listed. Forest Park Hampton hold is cancelled. Working plan: Amtrak in, cousin dinner downtown Friday, rideshare to the art museum Saturday, and store bags at Drury before the Sunday train.

messages.content: New work trip: I’ve been asked to attend an arts policy convening in San Antonio Jan. 23-25. Tuesday welcome event around 6 p.m., full Wednesday program, Thursday wrap-up expected to end at noon. I’ll fly from Chicago, carry-on only, and I’d like no rental car. Can you compare flight-and-hotel pairings, including the official block hotel versus a nearby place with breakfast and practical room amenities? Return Thursday after lunch, but not a late-night arrival home.

I can put that together. Two quick checks: is the meeting in the River Walk/La Villita area, and do you have a lodging or airfare reimbursement ceiling I should keep in mind while comparing the block with nearby hotels?

Yes, River Walk cultural campus, near La Villita and the Briscoe side. Lodging is defensible up to about $235 pretax if it’s the block, but lower is better. Airfare under $550 unless the timing is clearly better. Refundable hotel is preferred while the agenda firms up.

Here are the cleanest current pairings, assuming rideshare SAT-downtown both ways at about $55-65 total and no rental car:

| Pair | Tuesday arrival | Hotel | Thursday return | Est. all-in total | Main trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|
| A. Block + United | ORD 12:50 p.m. → SAT 3:46 p.m. nonstop | Hotel Contessa block, about $526 for 2 nights with tax | United 2:05 p.m. → ORD 4:57 p.m. nonstop | ~$932 | Best meeting access; breakfast extra; fridge is by request |
| B. Hampton Riverwalk + United | Same United outbound | Hampton Inn & Suites Riverwalk, about $397 with tax | Same United return | ~$803 | 7-9 min walk to venue; breakfast included; room basics stronger |
| C. Home2 Riverwalk + Southwest | MDW 10:40 a.m. → SAT 1:35 p.m. nonstop | Home2 Suites Riverwalk, about $382 with tax | Southwest 3:20 p.m. → MDW 6:10 p.m. nonstop | ~$760 | Cheapest and roomy; Midway logistics for you, slightly farther walk |

Cancellation snapshots: block currently cancelable until Jan. 20, 6 p.m.; Hampton/Home2 until Jan. 22 late evening. Dinner access is easy for all three because they’re downtown/River Walk, though the block hotel has the strongest on-site restaurant setup.
For the Hampton, is breakfast definitely included, and do the rooms list both coffee and a refrigerator?

Yes on the listing I’m seeing: hot breakfast included, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, and microwave. The standard king room is showing as refundable at the lower total. It does not have a full-service restaurant in the hotel, but there are casual dinner options within a few blocks and River Walk restaurants nearby.
What about the block hotel? I’m willing to pay some premium if it removes friction, but I don’t want to discover there’s no early coffee or fridge.

The block hotel is the most frictionless for the meeting: essentially next door to the venue, on-site restaurant, lobby coffee/bar service, and easy networking if people gather there. Breakfast is not included; expect roughly $18-25 each morning if you eat there. In-room coffee is listed. The refrigerator is the weak point: standard rooms say mini-fridge available by request, not guaranteed unless the hotel confirms it.
Can you break out the Thursday flight options after noon? United is fine if it’s comparable, but timing matters more than airline.

Thursday options that preserve a noon wrap-up:

| Airline | Depart SAT | Arrive Chicago | Fare est. | Notes |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| United nonstop to ORD | 2:05 p.m. | 4:57 p.m. | $346 RT with Tue outbound | Best fit: enough lunch/transfer margin, home before evening |
| American via DFW | 1:40 p.m. | 5:35 p.m. | $294 RT | Cheaper, but connection risk and a tighter exit from the venue |
| Southwest nonstop to MDW | 3:20 p.m. | 6:10 p.m. | $318 RT | Most relaxed departure; Midway arrival may be less convenient |
| United later via IAH | 5:15 p.m. | 9:45 p.m. | $331 RT | Too much airport wait and later than needed |

If the wrap-up truly ends at noon, the 2:05 United gives about 90 minutes to finish, grab a quick lunch or snack, and rideshare to SAT.
Is Southwest from Midway worth the savings? I’m on the north side, so ORD is usually easier. The Tuesday welcome at 6 is the main risk.

For this trip, I’d lean ORD/United unless the fare gap grows. Southwest saves about $28 versus United and gives a slightly earlier Tuesday arrival, but the airport trade-off on both ends probably eats the benefit. The United 3:46 p.m. arrival should still work: SAT is close to downtown, so even with a modest delay you should reach the hotel before 5 p.m. if carry-on only.
Let’s compare just the block hotel and Hampton paired with the United flights. Add breakfast out for the block so I can see the real difference.

With the United nonstop itinerary and two rideshares:

| Choice | Flight | Hotel/taxes | Breakfast assumption | Transfers | Practical total | What you get |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Block hotel | $346 | $526 | ~$40 for two mornings | ~$60 | ~$972 | 2-3 min venue walk, on-site dining, best networking convenience; fridge needs confirmation |
| Hampton Riverwalk | $346 | $397 | $0 included | ~$60 | ~$803 | Saves about $169, includes breakfast, coffee, mini-fridge; 7-9 min venue walk |

The block premium is easiest to justify if the welcome event stays at the block hotel or if evening networking is important. If the program is mostly at the venue and you’re comfortable with a short downtown walk, Hampton is the more practical value.
Can you put a refundable hold on the Hampton, but leave the block decision pending until I confirm the Tuesday welcome location?

Yes. I put the Hampton Inn & Suites San Antonio Riverwalk on hold for Jan. 23-25, refundable standard king room, estimated $397 with taxes. Breakfast is included, and the room listing shows coffee maker, mini-fridge, and microwave. Cancellation is showing as Jan. 22 before midnight local time. I have not booked the block hotel and have not ticketed airfare.
Please add one-bed room and quiet away from the elevator if that can be noted.

Added: one-bed room confirmed as the held room type, with a quiet-room/away-from-elevator request attached. Next step is to confirm whether Tuesday’s welcome stays at the block hotel or moves elsewhere; once that’s clear, the United 12:50 p.m. outbound and 2:05 p.m. Thursday return are the leading flight pair.

messages.content: San Antonio update: the organizer confirmed Wednesday and the Thursday wrap-up are staying at the River Walk venue, but Tuesday’s welcome moved to Centro de Artes. The block deadline is tomorrow morning. Can you do a final block hotel versus Hampton comparison before I decide? Airfare can wait until the hotel is settled.

Final lodging comparison based on that update:

| Hotel | 2-night total | Venue + welcome access | Breakfast / room basics | Dining / cancellation / transfers |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Hotel Contessa block | ~$526 with tax | 2-3 min walk to Wed/Thu venue; Centro de Artes is about 0.8 mi, so I’d rideshare after dark | Breakfast not included; in-room coffee listed; mini-fridge by request, not guaranteed in the standard room | On-site restaurant and River Walk dining; cancel by Jan. 20, 6 p.m.; airport rideshare same as Hampton |
| Hampton Riverwalk hold | ~$397 with tax | 7-9 min walk to Wed/Thu venue; Centro de Artes is about 0.5 mi, short rideshare or manageable walk | Breakfast included from about 6 a.m.; coffee, mini-fridge, microwave listed; one king held | No full-service restaurant, but several casual places nearby; cancel by Jan. 22 late evening; airport rideshare same |

Recommendation: keep Hampton unless the organizer says the block hotel is essential for after-hours networking. It saves about $129 on lodging, more like $160+ after breakfast, and the welcome move actually weakens the block hotel advantage.
Do we know if the Contessa fridge can be confirmed if I book the block?

Not from the block listing alone. It says mini-fridge available on request. I would call the hotel if you want to book it, but I’d treat it as uncertain until they attach it to the reservation. Coffee is listed in-room; breakfast would be restaurant or coffee bar, not included.
The Hampton room held is one bed, not two doubles, right? I don’t need a sofa bed if that’s the only king option.
Correct: the held room is a standard king, one bed. The listing may mention a work area, but it is not a two-double room. I also added the quiet/away-from-elevator request to that hold.
For the welcome event, would you have me walk back from Centro de Artes or just take a quick car?

I’d plan a short rideshare back, especially if it ends after dark or if you’re carrying materials. It should be roughly 5-8 minutes and inexpensive. Even adding that ride, Hampton still stays well below the block total.
Any hidden downside with Hampton besides the extra walk to the venue?

Main downsides: no on-site full-service restaurant, a little less convening atmosphere, and you’ll build in a few extra minutes each morning. Otherwise it fits the trip well: breakfast is handled early, coffee/fridge are clearer, cancellation is more flexible, and airport transfers are essentially identical.
Then keep Hampton and don’t book the block. Please make sure the hold is actually confirmed before the block deadline passes.

Confirmed. Hampton Inn & Suites San Antonio Riverwalk is the lodging plan for Jan. 23-25: refundable standard king, estimated $397 with taxes, breakfast included, in-room coffee, mini-fridge, and microwave listed, quiet-room request attached. No block booking needed.
Great. Next step will be airfare; I’m still leaning toward the United return after 2 if the fare hasn’t jumped.

Noted. Airfare is still pending. The leading flight plan remains United ORD-SAT Tuesday 12:50 p.m. to 3:46 p.m., returning SAT-ORD Thursday 2:05 p.m. to 4:57 p.m., provided the fare is still in a reasonable range when you’re ready to ticket.
